aspects.says: An ISOServer listens on a port, accepts many client connections through a channel of a chosen kind, and hands each incoming message to its request listeners.
aspects.reason: it needs a listening socket and a connecting peer, and a graded run has no network

aspects.says: A request listener answers a request by sending back a copy of it with the response MTI and a response code, through the source the request came from.
A listener returns true only when it has dealt with the message, because the server offers the message to its listeners in turn until one returns true.
Traffic between the server and its clients can be protected by the channel the server uses.
aspects.reason: it needs a live TLS connection to show anything; TLS comes from a socket factory given to the channel, and a graded run has no peer
